overall: The AG found the Georgetown Select Board violated the Open Meeting Law by discussing a Charter Commission topic that was anticipated 48 hours ahead but omitted from the original notice; it ordered future compliance.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board discussed a Charter Commission topic at its March 26 meeting that was left off the notice posted 48 hours before.
allegations.key_passage: By discussing a topic that was anticipated 48 hours or more prior to the March 26 meeting but that was not included on the notice posted 48 hours prior to the meeting, the Board violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint noted the meeting was in a small room and not broadcast on cable TV; the AG treated this as unclear and not a stated violation.
allegations.key_passage: It is unclear whether this was intended as an additional allegation

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law (G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25).
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
